title: 8. Wonhyo's Hwajaeng Theory and the Principles of a Mutually Flourishing Economy
content:
This chapter explores how the structure of the Buddhist four-gate *hwajaeng* examined in Chapter 5 [7] can be applied to today's economic problems.

### 8.1. The Historical Unfolding of Hwajaeng Theory

Wonhyo's *hwajaeng* thought, systematized in the *Treatise on the Harmonization of Disputes in Ten Aspects* (十門和諍論), is a principle that acknowledges the partial truth each position holds while integrating them within a more comprehensive truth.

Binary (二項) *hwajaeng* corresponds to the multidimensional thinking (Mimesis) of Part I. Ternary (三項) *hwajaeng* corresponds to the circular thinking (Mythos) of Part I. Quaternary (四項) *hwajaeng* corresponds structurally to the four modes of correlative thinking of Part I—multidimensionality, circulation, empathy, and convergence.

### 8.2. The Hwajaeng Structure of Economic Theory

The economic problems humanity faces today are also, in the end, constructed as a quaternary relation of four economic theories. These thoughts each give a different answer to "what is justice," but seen through the eyes of *hwajaeng*, they are mutually complementary as one node (和) of the whole circulation.

The following table shows the relation between traditional economic theories and the four-gate *hwajaeng*.

**Table 9 [duplicate numbering in original]: The Relation between Traditional Economic Theories and the Four-Gate Hwajaeng**

| Thought | Core principle | Four gates | Season | Philosophical core |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Utilitarianism | The greatest happiness of the greatest number (efficiency) | Gate of Arising-and-Ceasing | Spring | The autonomous arising (起) of the seed — the bursting forth of individual vital force |
| Communitarianism | Shared values and social bonds | Gate of the Three Natures | Summer | The efficient expansion of the vessel-world (器) — maximizing phenomenal abundance |
| Social contractarianism | Rational procedure and fair agreement | Gate of Suchness | Autumn | Cessation into fair rules (適滅) — universal order and principle |
| Libertarianism | The individual's absolute ownership and freedom | Pure Land Gate | Winter | The faith (信) of the great vessel called "we" — fundamental bonds and one mind |

These four economic theories correspond exactly to the four-season circulation principle of *hwajaeng*. Freedom (spring): the economy begins only when individual creativity wells up. Efficiency (summer): resources must be allocated efficiently so that society as a whole grows abundant. Fairness (autumn): transparent rules are needed to resolve the conflicts of distribution. Solidarity (winter): at the end of every process there must be a communal rest of "we are one."

Furthermore, the correspondence with Eastern thought is striking. If the "principle (理)" of Neo-Confucianism is the fairness of social contractarianism, then the "compassion (慈悲)" of Buddhism is the warmth of communitarianism, and the "*wu-wei* (無爲)" of Daoism is the interference-free vitality of libertarianism.

### 8.3. Economic Hwajaeng Seen through Vessel (器) and Arising (起)

The conflicts of the modern economy come fundamentally from the difference between valuing the "vessel (器, institution and structure)" and valuing the "arising (起, creative energy)." Only when we understand the mutual complementarity of these two concepts from the perspective of *hwajaeng* can we resolve the opposition of economic theories.

- **[Utilitarianism (the arising/起 of spring)]** "It is good to enlarge the size of the pie contained in the whole vessel." It emphasizes outcome-centered efficiency.
- **[Communitarianism (the vessel/器 of summer)]** "We are not isolated vessels. Only within the great vessel (器) of community does the individual's life too meaningfully arise (起)." It emphasizes the human as a correlative being.
- **[Social contractarianism (the cessation/rules of autumn)]** "First comes a transparent contract (cessation) to which one can submit no matter who becomes the vessel's owner." It seeks the legitimacy of procedure.
- **[Libertarianism (the faith/信 of winter)]** "Let not the vessel (the vessel-world) carelessly violate the achievement (起) I have wrought." It gives top priority to the individual's creative energy.

### 8.4. The Expansion of Hwajaeng and the Mutually Flourishing Economy

The AI era makes the need for *hwajaeng* more urgent than in any age in history. The modern economy, buried only in the infinite expansion of "spring (utilitarianism)," has lost its "winter (libertarian rest)." AI maximizes this speed of summer and alienates the human.

The direction of a *hwajaeng* solution is as follows. First, acknowledge community (summer), but let it be known that it came from the individual's freedom (winter). Second, pursue efficiency (summer), but let it remain within the framework of a fair contract (autumn). Third, through *hwajaeng* by way of symmetry (對稱性), pursue a structure that acknowledges the validity of each theory while integrating them circularly. Fourth, the hyperconnective technology of the AI era becomes the material foundation of *hwajaeng* connection.

Only when we understand that the economy is not a frozen number but a "time of water" that circulates like the four seasons does sustainable peace finally arrive. When the four great engines of freedom, efficiency, fairness, and solidarity are integrated into a single one-mind (一心) economic model, the economy of the AI era is converted into a mutually flourishing economy (相生經濟).

### 8.5. The Hwajaeng of World Religions

Master Wonhyo's *hwajaeng* (和諍) is, beyond conflict within Buddhism, a universal meta-model applicable also to opposition among world religions. In particular, the three Abrahamic religions—Judaism, Christianity, and Islam—started from a single root but have historically collided fiercely. Seen from the perspective of *hwajaeng*, they share the essence (性) while colliding in the phenomenon (相).

From the *hwajaeng* perspective, these three religions are not wrong with respect to one another; they are correlative manifestations in which a single divinity (one mind) has revealed itself according to different epochal demands within the "time of water" that is history. What the three religions share is the divinity (性) contained within the "vessel-world (器)"—the vessel of scripture—and conflict arises when they cling to the shape (相) of that vessel.

The following table shows the relation between the three Abrahamic religions and the four-gate *hwajaeng*.

**Table 10: The Three Abrahamic Religions and the Four-Gate Hwajaeng**

| Religion | The season of hwajaeng | Core emphasis | The role of hwajaeng |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Judaism | Spring (the beginning of law) | The strictness of covenant and law (the rules of the vessel-world) | The starting point of communal order |
| Christianity | Summer (the expansion of love) | Faith and universal love (the spread of the dharma-vessel) | Maximizing the energy of love |
| Islam | Autumn (absolute submission) | Complete devotion to the one God (refuge into cessation) | Urging the return to essence |

Conflict among religions in the AI era, too, must be approached by the principle of *hwajaeng*. Beyond the exclusivity that "only my own path (起) is right," it is the message of *hwajaeng* to acknowledge that all paths are streams of water that flow, in the end, into a single great ocean (大洋).
